newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR STARTS THURSDAY FAIRLY STABLE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR STARTS THURSDAY FAIRLY STABLE.

text.p: HARARE, July 31 (Reuaer) - The Zimbabwe dollar was quoted fairly stable on the U.S. unit in early Thursday interbank trade but dealers said the market was likely to remain on shaky ground the rest of the week with most players still quoting wide bid/offer spreads.
"The dollar seems to be firming up slightly after we saw the central (Reserve) bank intervene this morning...things are rather quiet at the moment," commented one dealer.

"But definitely today and tomorrow we should continue to see wide spreads," he added, saying dealers were not quite sure which levels to take if they were to revert to the normal one-point spread without making losses.

He said the market needed to see a large injection of foreign to bring back stability to the local currency which went on a relentless fall last week on the back of a large import payment, compounded on Friday by a central bank statement that the unit was overvalued.

At around 0815 GMT the Zimbabwe dollar was trading at 11.5500/6000 on the U.S. dollar after closing at 11.5500/6500 the previous day but was quoted softer on sterling at 18.9965/19.0890 compared to 18.8700/19.0450.
It was at 6.3170/3430 from 6.2700/3260 against the mark but was firmer on the rand at 2.5065/5175 from 2.5475/5505.
